content.text: {"relation":"DIVERGENT","consensus_summary":"All four blind responses converge on the pearl as a symbol of supreme spiritual worth — primarily the Kingdom of Heaven/salvation (Matt 13:45-46), with common alternatives that the pearl is Christ himself, or (reversed) the Church/believer purchased by Christ, plus secondary senses of sacred truth not to be profaned (Matt 7:6), the glory of the New Jerusalem's gates (Rev 21:21), and a negative sense of worldly luxury (1 Tim 2:9; Rev 17-18).","book_summary":"The book identifies the pearl as the full moon — a single complete light marking an appointed month and its meeting/feast — and reads the twelve pearl gates of the New Jerusalem as corresponding to the twelve months (bearing the tribes' names). It explicitly notes, and sets aside, the common teaching (kingdom worth everything / Church purchased by Christ).","consensus_core_identification":"Pearl = the Kingdom of Heaven (or Christ/salvation) as a treasure of surpassing value worth surrendering everything to obtain.","book_core_identification":"Pearl = the full moon, the complete monthly light marking an appointed time; twelve pearls = twelve months.","core_relation":"CONTRADICTS","extension_relation":"DIFFERENT_REFERENT","boundary_disagreement":"Not a boundary dispute: the book does not narrow or broaden the 'supreme treasure' category; it substitutes an astronomical/calendrical referent (full moon / appointed month) for the value-treasure referent entirely.","material_contradiction":"The consensus holds that the pearl symbolizes the kingdom/Christ/salvation as supreme treasure; the book holds it symbolizes the full moon marking appointed months. These cannot both be the central identification in the same sense — the book's own common-view note acknowledges the consensus reading and replaces it. The twelve pearl gates, read by consensus as glory/entrance to the kingdom, are reclassified as a twelve-month calendrical structure.","rationale":"Every consensus response and every listed alternative (kingdom, Christ, Church/believer, sacred truth, heavenly glory, luxury) is a value- or holiness-based identification. The book's lunar/calendrical identification appears in none of them and directly displaces the central referent, which the book itself flags as the 'commonly taught' view it is departing from. Because the book replaces rather than sharpens the consensus core, this is DIVERGENT, not REFINED, and it is not NOVEL-without-contradiction because the book explicitly contests the consensus identification of the same texts (esp. Rev 21:21).","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"The strongest objection to classifying this as fully divergent is that the book's entry could be read as an additional layer atop, rather than a denial of, the treasure reading — Rev 21:21's twelve pearls plausibly invite a twelve-fold calendrical scheme (cf. Ps 104:19 'He appointed the moon for seasons'), and the entry's common-view note might signal supplementation. However, none of the printed verses actually connects a pearl to the moon (the Proverbs excerpts compare wisdom/a virtuous woman to rubies, and Prov 7:20/Job 26:9 show a moon link only via Hebrew wordplay invisible in the KJV excerpts), so the moon-pearl identification rests on suggestive but indirect evidence.","confidence":"high"}
